1) Story file verification - Read docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md and confirmed it matches the specification provided in the prompt exactly (same Acceptance Criteria, Requirements REQ-TEST-FIX-*, Implementation Notes, Configuration Options, and Definition of Done checklist). No changes from the previously-assessed version.
2) Implementation – ESLint rule and helpers - File: src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts - Defines the ESLint rule that validates and auto-fixes test traceability. - `meta.fixable` is set to `"code"`, enabling ESLint `--fix` behavior as required by the story. - Options type and schema include the configuration flags specified in the story: - `autoFixTestTemplate?: boolean;` (default true) - `autoFixTestPrefixFormat?: boolean;` (default true) - `testSupportsTemplate?: string;` - These options are wired into the rule implementation: - `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestTemplate, testSupportsTemplate })` handles file-level `@supports` template insertion. - `handleCallExpression(node, context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestPrefixFormat })` is invoked for `CallExpression` nodes (`it`/`test`), enabling malformed `[REQ-...]` prefix normalization when configured. - The rule’s JSDoc uses @supports referencing this story and its requirements: `@supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE`.
- File: src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts - File-LEVEL TEMPLATE (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) - `buildSupportsTemplateComment(customTemplate?)`: - Uses default content `"@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ"` when no custom template is passed, matching the story’s template example. - Wraps it in a multi-line JSDoc block with an explicit TODO line: ``` /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ ``` - This satisfies template structure, placeholder clarity, and non-inference (placeholders only). - `insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, customTemplate?)`: - Inserts the template at the top of the file, or immediately after a shebang line, using `fixer.insertTextBeforeRange`. - Only adds a comment; it does not touch any test implementation code, preserving behavior and formatting aside from the new comment. - `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestTemplate, testSupportsTemplate })`: - Scans existing comments; if any contain `@supports`, it reports nothing (no duplicate template). - If missing, reports `missingFileSupports` and provides a fixer *only* when `autoFixTestTemplate` is not false, which calls `insertSupportsTemplate`. - Never attempts to guess story paths or REQ IDs beyond placeholders, satisfying REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE and REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE.
- MALFORMED `[REQ-XXX]` PREFIX FIXES (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) - `normalizeReqId(raw: string)` and `normalizeReqPrefixInDescription(description: string)`: - Recognize REQ-like tokens (e.g., `REQ_TEST_FIX`, `req-lowercase`, `REQ-TEST-FIX` in various wrappers) in a test description string. - Normalize: - Spacing: `[ REQ-TEST-FIX ]` → `[REQ-TEST-FIX]`. - Delimiter: `[REQ_TEST_FIX]` → `[REQ-TEST-FIX]`. - Case: `[req-lowercase]` → `[REQ-LOWERCASE]`. - Delimiters: `(REQ-PAREN)` → `[REQ-PAREN]`. - If no REQ-like token is found or normalization is ambiguous, they return `null`, and no fix is proposed. - `createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(originalNode, newValue, sourceCode)`: - Rebuilds the string literal while preserving quoting style and surrounding syntax; only the literal’s contents change, satisfying the requirement to preserve test structure and formatting. - `handleItOrTestCall(node, context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestPrefixFormat })`: - Identifies `it`/`test` calls with string literal descriptions. - When a malformed-but-recognizable REQ prefix is present and `autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false`, reports and provides a fixer that uses the normalized prefix. - When *no* REQ prefix exists, it reports `missingReqPrefix` but does **not** provide a fix, ensuring it never invents an ID or prefix (REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE and Error Handling).
3) Tests for this story - File: tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - JSDoc header: ```ts /** * @supports docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT * @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE */ ``` - Explicitly ties this test file to Story 021.0 and all its REQ-TEST-FIX-* requirements.
- Under `require-test-traceability` → `valid` cases: - Contains a test where the file already has a correct `@supports` block and a properly-formed `[REQ-TRACE-123]` test name, ensuring that no auto-fix is applied when not needed (verifying safe, non-intrusive behavior).
- Under `require-test-traceability` → `invalid` cases: - Missing file-level `@supports`: - Input: file without `@supports`, but with a valid `[REQ-ONE]` prefix on the test. - Expected output: same code but with the placeholder JSDoc `@supports` block (with TODO line) inserted at the top. - Confirms File-Level Template insertion, Template Quality, Quality Standards, Integration with ESLint’s `fix` (RuleTester uses ESLint’s fixer), and preservation of test behavior.
- Malformed REQ prefixes (all wired to REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT / SAFE / PRESERVE): - `[ REQ-TEST-FIX ]` → `[REQ-TEST-FIX]`. - `[REQ_TEST_FIX]` → `[REQ-TEST-FIX]`. - `[req-lowercase]` → `[REQ-LOWERCASE]`. - `(REQ-PAREN)` → `[REQ-PAREN]`. - In each case, the RuleTester `output` matches the expected normalized prefix, and everything else in the string and test body remains unchanged.
- No REQ prefix present: - Case: `it('missing prefix', () => {});` with a valid `@supports` above. - The test asserts that an error is reported but no `output` (autofix) is provided, confirming the rule does not fabricate `[REQ-XXX]` prefixes (REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE and Error Handling acceptance criteria).
- From the jest verbose run already executed: - We see the test file being executed and passing: - `PASS tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts` - Section: ``` require-test-traceability rule (Stories 020.0 and 021.0) require-test-traceability valid ✓ /** ... @supports docs/stories/020.0 ... */ describe('Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION', ...) (2 ms) invalid ✓ describe('Story 020.0...', ...) (3 ms) ... malformed prefix cases... ``` - Confirms that all coverage for Story 021.0’s behavior is exercised in the current code.
4) Test execution (project-wide) - Command run: `npm test -- --verbose`. - Exit code: 0. - Summary from the captured output: - Test Suites: 40 passed, 40 total - Tests: 302 passed, 302 total - Confirms tests for `require-test-traceability` (including all 021.0 auto-fix scenarios) are still passing in the latest codebase.
5) Documentation - user-docs (for the traceability plugin and its rules) include a documented description of `traceability/require-test-traceability`: - Explains that with ESLint `--fix`, the rule will: - Insert a file-level `@supports` placeholder JSDoc comment at the top of test files when it’s missing, including a TODO line telling developers to fill in story path and requirement IDs. - Normalize malformed `[REQ-XXX]` prefixes in test names (spacing, underscores vs hyphens, case, parentheses) without altering the semantic behavior of tests. - Documents the configuration options `autoFixTestTemplate`, `autoFixTestPrefixFormat`, and `testSupportsTemplate`, matching the story’s configuration section, thereby satisfying the Documentation acceptance criterion.
6) Acceptance criteria mapping - File-Level Template: Implemented via `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation` + `insertSupportsTemplate`; verified by helpers code and RuleTester invalid case expecting the placeholder `@supports` JSDoc block. - Format Fixes: Implemented via `normalizeReqId`/`normalizeReqPrefixInDescription` and `handleItOrTestCall`; malformed prefix patterns in the story (spacing, `_` vs `-`, case, parentheses) are all covered in tests and pass. - Template Quality: Template uses a placeholder story path and REQ IDs plus an explicit TODO line instructing developers to replace them; confirmed in helper implementation and expected output snapshots. - Quality Standards: Only annotations and string literal prefixes are changed; tests verify behavior is limited to these elements and that correctly formatted code is left unchanged. - Integration: Implemented as part of an ESLint rule with `meta.fixable: "code"` and used via ESLint’s standard `--fix` flow; RuleTester confirms integration. - User Experience: Templates are consistent across files; malformed prefixes are normalized to a single canonical format; behavior is deterministic and documented. - Error Handling: Fixers are only offered in unambiguous cases (when a REQ-like token is present); missing prefixes are reported without fixes; ambiguous cases short-circuit, ensuring only guaranteed-safe fixes. - Documentation: Rule behavior and configuration (including auto-fix and template format) are described in user documentation, aligning with the acceptance criterion.
Given that the story file matches the spec, the implementation directly addresses all listed requirements, tests explicitly cover the described auto-fix behaviors and are passing, and documentation is present, all acceptance criteria and Definition of Done items for this story are satisfied.
